analysis: The PR modifies only a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2ProductionWiringTests.swift. Changes: (1) line 312 test helper `recordServerStream` now handles `.toolCallDelta` alongside `.toolCall`, matching a new event case; (2) `makeThinkProbeEngine` (head ~1308-1322) takes a `modelType` parameter, defaulting to "qwen3_next"; (3) a new parameterized test at head ~1363-1389 for "qwen3_5"/"qwen3_5_moe" with a plain prompt tail keeps close-only reasoning output undecided. The tests use scripted in-process stub engines, a stub tokenizer, and a stub container, with no network, real keys, weights, or production code paths. I saw no changes to production code in the supplied units. The supplied base text (lines 1819-2472) is unchanged context: forged-schema rejection, VLM media bypass of the bridge, fail-loud no-engine backstop, cancellation propagation, heartbeat KV fallback reason clamping, and prefill deadline config. Those tests assert existing security-relevant behaviors (e.g. media requests not entering the text path, the heartbeat reason length clamp, and cancellation reaching the engine). They are not weakened by the visible patch. The new tests add coverage and do not remove assertions. No new attack surface, secrets, or trust-boundary changes. Threat T-041 (prefix cache) is not touched. Remaining question for integration: the production-side change that introduced `.toolCallDelta` and the Qwen3.5 reasoning-parser behavior is not in the supplied units, so I cannot assess its security implications (e.g. tool-call streaming handling or parser correctness). The patch excerpt is truncated at the new test, so the tail of the new test body was not visible.
